'''Fredrik "Fred" Zachariasen''' (1931–1999) was an American theoretical physicist, known for his collaborative work with [[Murray Gell-Mann]],<ref name="Gell-MannZachariasen1961">{{cite journal|last1=Gell-Mann|first1=Murray|last2=Zachariasen|first2=Fredrik|title=Form Factors and Vector Mesons|journal=Physical Review|volume=124|issue=3|year=1961|pages=953–964|issn=0031-899X|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.124.953|url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/4570/1/GELpr61b.pdf|bibcode=1961PhRv..124..953G}}</ref> [[Sidney Drell]],<ref name="DrellFriedman1956">{{cite journal|last1=Drell|first1=S. D.|last2=Friedman|first2=M. H.|last3=Zachariasen|first3=F.|title=Theory of ''S''-Wave Pion Scattering and Photoproduction at Low Energies|journal=Physical Review|volume=104|issue=1|year=1956|pages=236–248|issn=0031-899X|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.104.236|bibcode=1956PhRv..104..236D|url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/5824/|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and others.

==Early life and education==

Fredrik Zachariasen was born in 1931 in [[Chicago, Illinois]]. His father was the physicist [[William Houlder Zachariasen]].{{citation needed|date=July 2022}}

Fredrik Zachariasen graduated in 1951 with BS in physics from the [[University of Chicago]]<ref name=PT>{{cite journal|author=Baker, Marshall|author2=Ball, James S.|author3=Goldberger, Marvin|title=Fredrik Zachariasen|journal=Physics Today|volume=53|issue=7|date=July 2000|pages=69–70|doi=10.1063/1.1292490|doi-access=free}}</ref> and in January 1956 with PhD from [[Caltech]] with thesis ''Photodisintegration of the deuteron''.<ref>{{cite thesis|title=Photodisintegration of the deuteron|website=Caltech THESIS, Caltech Library Service|url=https://thesis.library.caltech.edu/2041/|year=1956|publisher=California Institute of Technology|type=phd}}</ref> He was a postdoc from 1955 to 1956 at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]], from 1956 to 1957 at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], and from 1957 to 1958 at [[Stanford University]], where he was an assistant professor from 1958 to 1960. 

==Career==
In 1960 he joined the faculty of Caltech and remained there until he retired in September 1999 as professor emeritus.<ref name=PT/> In 1960 he was a [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Sloan Research Fellow]].

He was a founding member of the [[JASON Defense Advisory Group]], where he worked with [[Walter Munk]] on acoustic detection of submarines.

{{blockquote|At a memorial service at the [[Athenaeum at Caltech|Athenaeum]] January 9, Zachariasen’s colleagues, friends, and family celebrated his life: his work in physics, his wide-ranging interests, his love of travel, of the outdoors, of good conversation, good food and, especially, good wine, and his passion to “solve the world.”<ref>{{cite journal|title=Fredrik Zachariasen (1931–1999)|journal=Science & Engineering Magazine of the Caltech Alumni Association|year=1999|volume=# 4|pages=41–42|url=http://calteches.library.caltech.edu/676/02/Obituaries.pdf}}{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>}}

===Ball-Baker-Zachariasen (BBZ) formulation===
{{blockquote|In a long series of papers and a review article, Baker, Ball, Zachariasen ... and co-workers have postulated a dual form of [[quantum chromodynamics|QCD]] in the continuum. Their formulation describes a non-Abelian dual superconductor and hence it confines color. They have calculated flux tubes, static quark potentials, temperature dependent effects and many other quantities in the [[N-body simulation#Tree methods|tree approximation]].<ref>{{cite arXiv|last=Haymaker |first=Richard W. |title=Dual Abrikosov vortices in U(1) and SU(2) lattice gauge theories|year=1995|eprint=hep-lat/9510035 }}</ref>}}

==Later life and legacy==
Fredrik Zachariasen's wife Nancy worked as a staff member at the library at the [[California Institute of Technology]]. They had two daughters. He died in 1999 in [[Pasadena, California]].{{citation needed|date=July 2022}}

Zachariasen's papers are held in the collection of the California Institute of Technology.<ref name="Archive">[https://oac.cdlib.org/findaid/ark:/13030/kt3t1nd0v4/admin/#prefercite-1.2.4 Fredrik Zachariasen Papers], 10195-MS, Caltech Archives, California Institute of Technology.</ref>
